title: Chapter 7: Tripura Polity — Constitution, Governance & Administration

blocks.content: Tripura has special provisions under the Indian Constitution, primarily to protect its tribal population, which has historically faced demographic and cultural pressure from the influx of Bengali settlers.

items: Sixth Schedule of the Constitution: Tripura is covered under the Sixth Schedule, which provides for creation of Autonomous District Councils for tribal areas with legislative, judicial, and administrative powers

Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC): Created under the Sixth Schedule in 1985; covers 68.1% of Tripura's geographical area (but with lower population density); has its own legislature and executive
Inner Line Permit: Tripura does NOT have ILP (unlike Arunachal Pradesh); this is a major difference from other NE states
Article 371 series: No specific Article 371 provision for Tripura unlike some NE states
Land Rights: Tribal land alienation is regulated; non-tribals cannot easily buy land in scheduled tribal areas

blocks.content: 7.2 Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC)

The TTAADC is one of the most significant institutions in Tripura's governance structure. Established in 1985 under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, it provides tribal communities a degree of self-governance.

cells: 68.1% of Tripura's geographical area (but less than 30% of population as tribal areas are sparsely populated)
Can make laws on subjects: land management, forests (not reserved), water, social customs, money lending, matrimony, tribal festivals
Yes — TTAADC has its own security force for internal enforcement
Receives grants from state and central government
Protects tribal land rights; regulates land use in tribal areas; provides education and social services to tribes
State government has overriding powers; TTAADC laws need Governor's approval
Elected by the council from among members; called Executive Member (EM) or Chief Executive Member
Controlled by TIPRA Motha (new tribal party, 2022 onwards) under Pradyot Kishore Manikya Debbarman
10 members or 1/6 of total — whichever is greater
First CM of Tripura; dominated early politics
20 years as CM; known for simplicity; no personal car for many years; one of India's poorest CMs; Tripura literacy soared under him; awarded best CM in Northeast
BJP's first CM in Tripura; ended Left's 25-year rule; controversial statements; development focus
Dental surgeon; Rajya Sabha MP; became CM 2022; won 2023 elections; continuity of BJP governance

items: 8 Districts, each headed by a District Magistrate/Collector (IAS)
58 Blocks (Panchayat Samiti level) headed by Block Development Officer (BDO)
Rural areas: Gram Panchayats — approx. 1,200 GPs
Urban bodies: Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC); Dharmanagar, Udaipur, Ambassa, Belonia Municipal Councils
TTAADC: Covers tribal areas; Khumulwng HQ; own governance structure
Tripura Police: DGP at top; 2 ranges (North and South); SP at district level; Armed Police Battalions — Tripura State Rifles (TSR)
Tripura State Rifles (TSR): State armed police; played major role in counter-insurgency in 1980s-2000s; now mainly for law and order
